newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel weakens against dollar, basket.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel weakens against dollar, basket.

text.p: The Israeli shekel's representative rate was fixed slightly lower against the dollar and the basket of key foreign currencies on Wednesday following the U.S. currency's rise abroad, dealers said.

"The dollar rose in Europe following the 25-basis-point rate increase of the Federal Reserve. In local trading the shekel declined mildly following the rise of the dollar," said a dealer at Bank Hapoalim.
"The basket rose slightly and the Bank of Israel did not need to intervene today," the dealer said.
The central bank has been intervening regularly in the market to defend the basket of foreign currencies, which has been trading at the bottom end of its band for two months.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.3700 shekels against 3.3660 on Tuesday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.6592 shekels against 3.6574 on Tuesday.
On the crosses, the shekel traded against the yen at 2.7131 shekels per 100 yen compared with 2.7245 on Tuesday, and against the mark at 1.9931 shekels after 1.9959 on Tuesday.
In the late afternoon, the dollar was trading at 3.3700 shekels.
